stream.scotty.core.windowFunction.builtin

Class Max<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>

  • java.lang.Object
    • stream.scotty.core.windowFunction.builtin.Max<InputType,ValueType>
  • Type Parameters:
    InputType - type of the input tuples
    ValueType - type of the compared values
    All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable, AggregateFunction<InputType,ValueType,ValueType>, CommutativeAggregateFunction<InputType,ValueType,ValueType>

    public class Max<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>
extends Object
implements CommutativeAggregateFunction<InputType,ValueType,ValueType>
    Maximum of the values in a window. Works for all Comparable values, e.g. numbers or strings. Max is not invertible, Scotty recomputes the aggregate if a tuple has to be removed from a slice.

    Use create() if the input tuples are the values, or Max(ValueExtractor) to use a value extracted from each input tuple.

    See Also:

      • lift

        public ValueType lift(InputType inputTuple)
        Description copied from interface: AggregateFunction
        Transforms a tuple to a partial aggregate. For example, consider an average computation. If a tuple ⟨p,v⟩ contains its position p and a value v, the lift function will transform it to ⟨sum←v, count←1⟩, which is the partial aggregate of that one tuple.
        Specified by:
        lift in interface AggregateFunction<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>
        Parameters:
        inputTuple - input Tuple
        Returns:
        PartialAggregate

      • combine

        public ValueType combine(ValueType partialAggregate1,
                         ValueType partialAggregate2)
        Description copied from interface: AggregateFunction
        Computes the combined aggregate from partial aggregates. Each incremental aggregation step results in one call of the combine function. It is expected that this method returns new partial aggregate. This method is used in two ways. 1. To add a single element to the partial aggregate. 2. To merge two big partial aggregates (or slices) , for example for emitting a final window. For the second step it is needed to emit a completely new partial aggregate. This can involve a deep copy of the partial aggregates. To prevent this a AggregationFunction can implement CloneablePartialStateFunction. In this case copy provides a cloned partial aggregate as the first argument.
        Specified by:
        combine in interface AggregateFunction<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>
        Parameters:
        partialAggregate1 - the first original partial aggregate or a cloned object iff the AggregationFunction implements CloneablePartialStateFunction
        partialAggregate2 - the second ordinal partial aggregate.
        Returns:
        combined PartialAggregate

      • lower

        public ValueType lower(ValueType aggregate)
        Description copied from interface: AggregateFunction
        Transforms a partial aggregate to a final aggregate. In our example, the lower function computes the average from sum and count: ⟨sum, count⟩ 7→ sum/count.
        Specified by:
        lower in interface AggregateFunction<InputType,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>,ValueType extends Comparable<? super ValueType>>
        Returns:
        final Aggregate
